note: Pass with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the battery was administered in Dutch to a Dutch community sample, but no Dutch VFQ-25 wording exists in the deposit (DataverseNL doi:10.34894/CMJXAK -- only Data_total.csv, Data_test_retest.csv and two variable-information files, whose sole VFQ entries read 'VFQ;National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire - 25 (NEI-VFQ-25)' and 'VFQ.A;... Appendix', with no per-item labels) nor in the PLOS ONE article's S1-S4 appendices (which carry the SVC only). Base fields therefore hold the instrument publisher's ENGLISH, language=Dutch, _translated columns empty: text_source=translated_substitute. (2) FORMAT: the study administered the battery online, so the SELF-administered RAND form was used rather than the interviewer-administered one; its wording differs only in the preamble and in the absence of '(READ CATEGORIES AS NEEDED)' directives. The three general preamble paragraphs are shipped as instructions; the form's six numbered administration instructions ('give it to a member of the project staff. Do not take it home') and its statement of confidentiality are NOT shipped, as they describe a paper session at a study centre that this online administration did not have. Options still read 'Circle One' on the source form; that framing is not reproduced in any shipped field. (3) resp IS NOT THE RAW RESPONSE CATEGORY. The deposit stores the RAND-converted 0-100 item scores, and data/neurodegenerative_huizinga_2019.R rescales 0/25/50/75/100 -> 0/1/2/3/4 and, for VFQ.2, 0/20/40/60/80/100 -> 0/1/2/3/4/5, so higher resp = BETTER vision-related functioning and the option order is the REVERSE of the printed 1..5/1..6 numbering for items 1-14, 15c, 16, 16a and the SAME as printed for 17-25. The printed sixth option of the difficulty items ('Stopped doing this for other reasons or not interested in doing this') is set to missing by RAND scoring and so has no row. VFQ.15, VFQ.15a and VFQ.15b are unscored skip-logic items and keep their raw 1/2 and 1/2/3 codes. (4) VFQ.15c ANOMALY: the printed 15c offers only four options (No difficulty..Extreme difficulty), yet 7 of 1,089 respondents have resp=0, one level below 'Extreme difficulty'. option_text is left blank for that row rather than guessed; the most likely reading is that the Dutch online form reused the 'stopped because of your eyesight' option from the neighbouring driving items 16/16a. (5) Interviewer read-aloud artefacts are transcribed literally rather than tidied: item 3's last option prints as 'All of the time?' and item 4's as 'Severe, or' / 'Very severe?'. (6) RIGHTS: no restriction. The questionnaire's own cover page states 'RAND hereby grants permission to use the "National Eye Institute Visual Functioning Questionnaire 25 (VFQ-25) July 1996"' and '5. No further written permission is needed for use of this NEI VFQ-25 - July 1996'; condition 4 expressly contemplates 'printing and distributing this document' subject to a credit line acknowledging that it was developed at RAND under the sponsorship of the National Eye Institute, which is an attribution requirement and not a reserved right. RAND's survey page adds 'The VFQ-25 is a public document available without charge to all researchers' and 'All of the surveys from RAND Health Care are public documents, available without charge.' No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears on the cover page, the FAQ or the RAND page. (7) Step 3b: the live data is 29 items VFQ.1-VFQ.25 plus the irregular VFQ.15a/15b/15c/16a driving sub-items, exactly the VFQ-25's own numbering, and matches no sibling instrument in this battery; the 13 optional appendix items VFQ.A1-A13 the study also administered are excluded by the processing script and are not in this table.
public_note: Item text is the NEI VFQ-25's official ENGLISH wording; the study administered the questionnaire in Dutch and neither the paper's appendices nor the DataverseNL deposit publish the Dutch form, so this is a same-instrument substitute rather than what respondents read. Note also that resp is the RAND-converted 0-100 item score rescaled (higher = better vision-related functioning), not the response number printed on the questionnaire, so for items 1-14, 15c, 16 and 16a the option order is the reverse of the printed one.
